speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; tell me, what specific symptoms are you noticing, such as rapid breathing, grunting, or flaring of the nostrils? Have there been any complications during your birth, and is your mother's history relevant to this situation?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS). The history of prematurity (32 weeks) and maternal gestational diabetes are classic risk factors for RDS due to surfactant deficiency. I am requesting a Chest_X-Ray to confirm the characteristic ground-glass appearance.
